newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent bounces back into black ahead of APIs.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent bounces back into black ahead of APIs.

text.p: IPE oil futures bounced back sharply on Tuesday afternoon led by U.S. gasoline ahead of weekly inventory data and some short-covering ahead of the expiry today of the June NYMEX crude contract.
Dealers said the spark for the price rise was news that Turkish Kurdish rebels had attacked a small oil installation in southeast Turkey.
July Brent stood up 17 cents at $20.33 a barrel by 1530 GMT, up from a low for the day of $19.84
"The news itself was minor but it provided a spark and took it through resistance at $20.08," said a broker. "Now it's testing $20.36."
Brent fell earlier on Tuesday as fears mounted that U.S. refiners would not want to take delivery of foreign crudes against the expiry of June NYMEX crude.
"That doesn't seem to be a concern anymore," said a broker.
Dealers said the market now was focused on Tuesday evening's American Petroleum Institute report. "Maybe there's a feeling the APIs will be bullish for gasoline," said a trader.
Last week the API showed crude stocks rose a huge seven million barrels to stand in advance of year-ago levels. Oil markets, ignoring the data, promptly shot up.
June IPE gas oil on Tuesday also recovered up $1.00 to $178.75 but the July crack spread remained at a depressed $3.88 a barrel.
